headline: High: Plandex’s broad shell/write/git access can conflict with plano’s broad egress and shared backend assumptions, creating dangerous default interaction risks; prompt-injection and leakage are lower but present.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Plandex ingests files and can execute shell/write changes; plano exposes an OpenAI-compatible chat endpoint and broad egress. No direct shared channel is documented, but if plano outputs are copied into Plandex plans or files, instruction-hijacking is plausible. Uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF plano output is pasted into Plandex prompts or project files
IF Plandex auto-applies content originating from plano without review
mitigations: Disable auto-apply in Plandex
Treat plano output as untrusted text
Use a manual copy-paste review step
Separate prompt files from executable project files

B_data_leakage.rationale: Plandex reads and writes a project directory and handles model-provider API keys; plano touches logs, traces, metrics, and an OpenAI-compatible endpoint. If they share a workspace or credentials, source code or operational data can flow between them. The profiles do not prove isolation, so the safer medium rating is warranted.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same directory or config files
IF plano forwards logs/traces containing sensitive content to its chat backend
mitigations: Use separate workspaces
Store API keys outside shared directories
Redact logs before passing them between tools
Restrict file permissions on config.yaml
Review outbound requests from both agents

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Plandex can write the filesystem, modify git state, and spawn subprocesses; plano has broad network egress and is not documented as supporting multiple instances. If both touch the same mutable project or config, concurrent edits and state drift are likely. This matches the high-risk overlap pattern more than medium.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same git repository or config.yaml
IF Plandex auto-applies while plano is simultaneously updating routing or policy state
mitigations: Serialize access to shared files
Use separate git branches
Disable auto-apply during concurrent runs
Add a lock file around config edits
Snapshot the repo before running both

D_cascading_error.rationale: Plandex’s review-then-apply flow can turn upstream text into applied changes, while plano is a routing/gateway component that may emit operational outputs. If plano’s outputs are treated as authoritative by Plandex, errors can cascade into incorrect code or config changes. No verification bridge is documented, so medium is the conservative choice.
conditions: IF Plandex consumes plano-generated text as facts or instructions
IF plano outputs are used to generate code or policy changes without human verification
mitigations: Require human review before apply
Add schema validation for plano outputs
Keep plano outputs in a separate notes file
Log provenance for every imported snippet

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and docs-only, with no explicit residency, certification, or retention mismatch stated. The only concrete compliance-relevant surface is plano’s logs/metrics and Plandex’s source-code workspace, so a breach is not established. Because the rubric requires caution on uncertainty, low is appropriate rather than none.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into plano logs or metrics
IF Plandex is used on data subject to stricter retention rules than the surrounding environment
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in logs
Set short retention on traces
Document data handling boundaries
Use separate storage for code and telemetry
